answer: Radio fingerprints anchor each identity to its handset: flaws in the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth front end give every chip a unique signature, hashed at enrollment. Each epoch a fresh challenge forces re-measurement through a rotating verifier, so one recording cannot serve many identities. Faking one costs a radio, so attacker cost scales linearly, and a marble-smooth emulator fails for lacking the noisy quirks of real silicon. Limits: drift after repairs, and a relic handset that swaps its radio must re-enroll; pair with random liveness checks and slashing of verifiers that approve duplicates.
